newsitem.title: USA: Dataquest sees drop in semiconductor revs this yr.
newsitem.headline: Dataquest sees drop in semiconductor revs this yr.

text.p: Worldwide revenues for the semiconductor industry are expected to drop more than nine percent this year, according to a revised study released Tuesday.

Dataquest, a computer research firm, said worldwide semiconductor market revenues are expected to fall to $137 billion this year, compared with an earlier forecast that predicted a drop of only 7.6 percent.
Dataquest attributed the revised forecast to a variety of factors, including heavy inventories and falling prices for dynamic random access memory chips.

"Although end-equipment markets slowed in 1996, the major causes of the decline were excess inventories, excess capacity, a DRAM price collapse, and a weakening yen," said Gary Grandbois, vice president and chief analyst in Dataquest's Semiconductors Worldwide program.
However, while the semiconductor market has taken a negative slide, Dataquest said the worst may be over.
"With the end-equipment markets firming up in 1997 and an end to the memory price slide, we expect 1997 to be a growth year for the industry."

In recent months, the semiconductor's key demand indicator -- the book to bill ratio -- has shown improvement, leading analysts to predict the market is starting to rebound. In September the book to bill ratio hit 0.99, the highest level this year.

Dataquest said all of the major regions of the world will suffer large revenue declines this year but Japan will see the largest decline in 1996 because the yen-to-dollar exchange rate continues to decline rapidly as compared to 1995.
